correctness.rationale: The quantified all-n group action is explicit. Splitting the graph cellular chain sequence over the 2-element twin-swapping characters proves the H1 representation, including exclusion of multi-flip characters. Each twin pair has identical closed Rips-2 neighborhoods, so twin swaps act contiguously to the identity; strong collapses reduce to the subdivision S(K_n). Its S_n-invariant contractible core has exactly C(n,3) triangular relative 2-cells, and permutations act on them by alternating signs, identifying H2 integrally with exterior-cube permutation lattice. At radius 3 a doubled vertex is a universal cone point. For n=5 an independent complete acyclic matching on 1413 nonempty faces leaves one vertex and ten triangles, and separate signed Lefschetz checks verify all 3840 group elements. No extrapolation of finite enumeration to n>5 is used.

originality.rationale: The full Adamaszek 2011 Section 5 supplies the nonequivariant scale-two homotopy of subdivided graphs, and the exact published 2026 S(K_n) record supplies the undoubled nonequivariant barcode. The inspected sources do not give the doubled graph family, the 2^n different flip-character behavior in H1, or the combined all-group degree-two character. A different published multiclique character formula concerns labeled multiedge CW cells, not graph-metric Rips complexes. Actual named claim and equivalent/reduced-object searches found no stronger covering statement. The natural equivariance of Adamaszek triangles is a meaningful residual risk to originality of the H2 term alone, but not a direct implication of the new whole two-degree semidirect persistence module.
residual_risks: An earlier equivariant graph-power/clique subdivision theorem may contain the exterior-cube identification implicitly or explicitly; the degree-two representation alone is therefore not claimed as the only new object.
The original Folkman 1967 article was not available in full; its uninspected sections are not treated as negative evidence.
An unindexed or differently worded calculation of the twin-swap graph-cycle representation or full group-valued persistence may exist.
Semantically similar sign representations on other complexes do not automatically establish this case but deserve review.

value.rationale: For the canonical semisymmetric Folkman graph and its natural all-n generalization, the full symmetry character of two successive persistence degrees determines what raw homology ranks cannot: exactly which graph cycles carry each independent pair-swap sign, why all pair-swaps become invisible at the next scale, the alternating triangle module under S_n, and zero global invariants in both stages. This is a structurally motivated family-wide equivariant persistence calculation, not an arbitrary graph enumeration or a routine re-labeling of the 2011 nonequivariant theorem. The two-stage representation change is a meaningful and reusable topological refinement.
